thread:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — Canary shows a memory regression for quant-v2 models on runtime-3.2 in eu region. Seen during longseq tests.
Maya Patel: ugh. which canary pool?
Alex Chen: eu-canary-2 (low qps), reproduces with 2 concurrent requests at ~1.2M tokens/session.
Samira Gomez: logs? stack traces?
Alex Chen: pasted snippet from node: `OOM after KV cache growth to 18GB`; full log: ```
2026-03-20T12:09:22Z node-34 runtime-3.2 quant-v2 session_id=... OOM at alloc kv_cache +18GB
```
Kevin Wu: this is new since the kernel switch in 3.2?
Alex Chen: seems correlated with kernel:attention-tiling change in runtime-3.2+quant path. Not seen on cpu fallback or runtime-3.1.
ops-sre: deploy-bot pinned runtime-3.2 for model-group=quant-v2 in eu at 2026-03-20T12:12Z :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: /pin runtime=3.2 scope=model-group:quant-v2 region=eu reason="memory-regression-canary" by ops-sre
Maya Patel: We need a decision: soft-pinback (keep 3.1 for quant-v2) or roll back kernel?
Samira Gomez: Prefer pinback for now — lower blast radius. We can investigate kernel rollback in parallel.
Kevin Wu: Agree. Operational plan: 1) update pinlist for eu-hosted quant-v2 to runtime=3.1 2) pause auto-unpin window 3) run extended canary profiling 4) patch release note and SDK compatibility guidance.
Maya Patel: I'll own the pinlist change and the unpin pause. Doing it now.
Maya Patel: `deploy-bot update-pin --region eu --model-group quant-v2 --runtime 3.1 --duration 72h --reason "canary mem regression"`
deploy-bot: Pin update queued: id=pin-8683 region=eu model-group=quant-v2 runtime=3.1 expires_in=72h requested_by=Maya Patel
Alex Chen: Samira, can you run the longseq profiling job against runtime-3.2 on a separate isolated pool? Add KV throttling to see if it's caching runaway.
Samira Gomez: On it. kicking off run job at 12:20Z. I'll share traces when done.
Maya Patel: Ops: please hold any scheduled canary unpins in eu for next 24h.
ops-sre: acknowledged — paused scheduled unpins for eu-canary pools until 2026-03-21T12:20Z.
Kevin Wu: Release notes / customer comms: we should add internal note: "runtime-3.2: soft-pin applied for quant-v2 on EU hosted due to memory regression during long sequences; no customer-facing changes yet; investigating kernel attention tiling." Also add an SDK compatibility blurb: "If you pin runtime in client SDK, expect runtime 3.1 availability to remain for quant-v2 in eu while we investigate."
Alex Chen: Samira, if you confirm it's kernel-related, we'll plan a kernel rollback in a canary region (non-EU) to validate fix speed vs pin length.
Samira Gomez: Preliminary trace points to kv_cache growth heuristic mis-trigger; not strictly kernel but interaction with tiling + kv prefetcher. I will add telemetry flags to reproduce.
Maya Patel: Routing: please add a temporary fallback policy so traffic to quant-v2 models in eu falls back to dedicated capacity if latency spikes/OOM risk. I can add that to the routing config.
Alex Chen: Good. Keep me posted. If the canary profiling clears, we'll lift pin early. If not, escalate to rollback.
Kevin Wu: Who's owner for rollout notes and ticket?
Maya Patel: I'll open RH-TICKET-3421 and draft the internal release note. Will update the ops runbook with rollback thresholds (>=3 OOMs in 1h across canary => rollback kernel).
Maya Patel: RH-TICKET-3421 created: https://redwood.internal/tickets/RH-TICKET-3421
deploy-bot: pin id=pin-8683 applied to live pinlist at 2026-03-20T12:25Z by Maya Patel
Samira Gomez: profiling job finished — attaching flamegraph link (internal): https://redwood.internal/trace/fg-12345
Samira Gomez: flamegraph shows KV cache allocation surge triggered by prefetcher loop at step ~2.4M tokens.
Alex Chen: Ok that's actionable. Samira, can you try disabling prefetcher on a patched runtime build (3.2-patch-prefetch-off) and run same job? We'll compare.
Samira Gomez: yes. launching pref-off build in non-eu-canary now. ETA 45m.
ops-sre: FYI — I've added an incident annotation to the release timeline and assigned on-call to monitor canary metrics.
Maya Patel: I'll also note in the internal release notes: "Action: soft-pin 72h; next steps: telemetry triage -> pref-off experiment -> kernel rollback plan if needed."
Kevin Wu: Thanks all. We'll reconvene in ~1h or when pref-off results come back. :calendar:
Alex Chen: Closing loop: pin applied, unpin paused, tickets created, experiments running. Good coordination.
Maya Patel: leaving the thread for follow-ups in RH-TICKET-3421. :white_check_mark:
